extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of classical/modern geometry; readers of mathematical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Classical results and constructive criteria for ruled surfaces (hyperboloid of one sheet, hyperbolic paraboloid) and analytic/variational criteria for the minimum-area circumscribing ellipse through given points/triangles/quadrilaterals. Includes related lemmas and dynamical formulae (moments of inertia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for a line to be a generatrix (construction from three directrices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given three directrices L1, L2, L3 and a point p on one directrix L1, a generatrix through p is obtained as the intersection of the two planes through p that respectively pass through the other two directrices; the intersection line rests on the given directrix and cuts or is parallel to the other directrices (cannot be parallel to both if those directrices are not parallel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct two planes: one through p and L2, another through p and L3; their intersection is the required generating line. The text explains why the intersection must cut or be parallel to L2 and L3 and thus satisfy the generatrix condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genesis of the hyperboloid of one sheet (construction rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take three straight lines, no two coplanar and not all three parallel to the same plane; let planes about two of them revolve so as always to intersect in the third line: the intersections of these revolving planes generate the hyperboloid of one sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an equivalent geometric description (genesis) of the ruled surface; the construction may be viewed in two symmetric modes leading to the same surface (different ensembles of generating lines/directrices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plane sections of a hyperboloid of one sheet are conic sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Any plane section of the hyperboloid of one sheet that does not coincide with a generatrix or a directrix is a conic section: the intersection points of generatrices with the section-plane lie on a single conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses anharmonic ratios of sines of angles between systems of planes through directrices, showing six points lie on the same conic; any four arbitrary generatrices determine the conic and any other generating line meets the section in the same conic point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section-plane coinciding with a directrix yields two straight-line section
rubrics_metrics.description: If the section-plane coincides with one of the directrices it also coincides with exactly one generatrix; the conic section degenerates to two straight lines (they meet if the plane does not pass through the centre, and are parallel if it does).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since every generatrix meets the directrix, revolving the plane about that directrix meets every generatrix successively; no plane through a directrix can avoid cutting the surface in a second straight line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-parallelism of generatrices through a directrix
rubrics_metrics.description: No two generatrices can be parallel; therefore in any given plane through a directrix at most one generatrix of the surface can lie in that plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate geometric restriction used in classifying plane sections and intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel parallels to generating lines form a cone (lemma and consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines drawn parallel to all generating lines of either system of a hyperboloid constitute an ordinary cone (right or oblique); if these parallels are all drawn through the same point as vertex, the cone is the same whichever system is chosen. Lemma: If four planes pass through the same line and parallel planes through a fixed point are drawn, these latter intersect in a line through that point parallel to the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration: draw planes through the given point parallel to the family of planes that generate the hyperboloid; their intersections give edges parallel to generatrices and the cone formed has analogous dihedral relations and similar section-figures to those of the hyperboloid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic cone from centre parallels
rubrics_metrics.description: When the parallels to the generatrices are drawn through the centre of the hyperboloid, the resulting cone is the asymptotic cone; sections of hyperboloid and cone by the same plane are concentric, similar, and similarly situated; their conjugate diameter systems coincide in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies a special cone related to asymptotes of the hyperboloid; further properties may be developed (author notes more discussion if space permits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbolic paraboloid genesis when directrices parallel to a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: If the three given directrices are all parallel to the same plane, the system reduces to three parallel planes and the generatrices become parallel to some determinate plane; the generated surface is the hyperbolic paraboloid (twisted plane).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two equivalent descriptions are given: (1) generated by a line moving upon three given directrices all parallel to a plane; (2) as a twisted plane: a line moving on two skew lines and always parallel to a given plane. The first is the systematic definition; the second is better viewed as a property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of the hyperbolic paraboloid (lines on surface)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hyperbolic paraboloid admits two distinct modes of description (two systems of generatrices); through any point on the surface two straight lines lying wholly on the surface may be drawn (never more than two); each line of one system meets every line of the other system; no two lines of the same system meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties mirror those of the hyperboloid of one sheet except where they depend on parallelism of directrices (parallelepiped degeneracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of the minimum-area ellipse through four given points (non-re-entrant quadrilateral)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quadrilateral whose vertices are four given points with no re-entering angle, there exists one and only one ellipse of minimum area passing through the four points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic method: choose coordinates (axes through intersection of two opposite sides), write general circumscribing conic with parameter z (coefficient of xy) and find z by minimizing area. The minimizing z is the unique real root of a derived cubic (equation (5)) lying between specified bounds; by root-sign analysis there is exactly one admissible root, hence a unique minimum ellipse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for curve to be an ellipse (in analytic parametrization)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the general circumscribing conic mm' x^2 + z xy + nn' y^2 - (...) x - (...) y + 1 = 0, with given parameters m,m',n,n', the curve is an ellipse provided z^2 < 4 m m' n n'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inequality appears when ensuring the quadratic form is positive definite (ellipse) after coordinate choices; z is then chosen within the admissible interval to minimize area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelogram special case — diagonals conjugate diameters
rubrics_metrics.description: If the quadrilateral is a parallelogram (special limit of the general case), the extremal equation reduces and shows the diagonals of the parallelogram are conjugate diameters of the minimal circumscribed ellipse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case certain parameters become negatives of each other and analytic simplification yields the admissible z showing conjugacy of diagonals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to triangle problem (limit) and tangent direction
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum-area ellipse described about three given points (triangle) is obtained as a limiting case of the four-point problem; for the minimum ellipse about triangle EDC touching a line through E in a given direction, the condition yields that the tangent at E is parallel to CD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take two vertices tending to coincide to form E; parameters tend to infinity with a preserved ratio, reducing the cubic to a quadratic whose admissible root determines the ellipse; further differentiation when allowing the touching direction to vary yields tangency parallelism and center location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center of minimum ellipse for triangle coincides with triangle centroid
rubrics_metrics.description: For the ellipse of minimum area circumscribing a given triangle, the center of that ellipse coincides with the centre of gravity of the triangle (centroid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both analytic reduction and an a priori geometric demonstration are given in the text; coordinates and parameter elimination show the centre reduces to the triangle's barycentric centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for least circumscribed ellipse using diagonals as axes (quadrilateral)
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing the diagonals of a quadrilateral as coordinate axes, express the ellipse equation in centered form with parameters L,M and inclination φ; the area formula depends on φ and must be minimized with respect to φ leading to a cubic in cos φ whose single admissible root between −1 and 1 gives the minimum-area orientation and thus the minimal ellipse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive center coordinates in terms of L,M,cosφ, compute principal semiaxes via a quadratic whose coefficients involve A,B,C (related to L,M,cosφ), then area = π m n; differentiate area formula wrt φ and solve cubic (equation (8)) for cos φ; choose the unique root in [−1,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: Moments of inertia of regular solids — equality of principal moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma: For any of the five regular solids, the principal moments of inertia A, B, C about axes through the centre are all equal; consequently the moments about all other axes through the centre are equal as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument by contradiction: assume unequal principal moments, derive impossible linear relation for cos^2 of direction cosines. This equality simplifies computation: partition solids into pyramids with common vertex at the centre and sum pyramid moments to obtain the solid's moment (independent of axis orientation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moment of inertia of a right pyramid about an inclined axis through the vertex (integral formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: The moment of inertia of a right pyramid (base any plane regular figure) about an axis through the vertex inclined at angle α to the pyramid axis equals the integral over laminae parallel to the base of [e i x^2 dx (cos^2 α) + i f i x^2 dx (1 + (1/ i f e)) sin^2 α], leading after integration to closed-form formulae used to derive moments for regular solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the pyramid as a stack of similar laminae; use known planar lamina moment relations and the parallel-axis decomposition; integrate from vertex to base and sum pyramid contributions for regular polyhedra by symmetry.
